name: psychology_journaling.json
description: Behavioural biases, journaling templates, routines and problem-gambling warning signs. Self-monitoring material, not therapy.
principle: Most account damage comes from behaviour (oversizing, revenge trading, rule-breaking), not from bad indicators. Rules written in advance beat decisions made under emotion.

biases.name: Revenge trading
biases.description: Trading harder to recover a loss.
biases.fix: Hard stop after 2 consecutive losses or daily cap; walk away for the day.

biases.name: FOMO
biases.fix: Only enter at predefined triggers; skip entries beyond 1.5-2 ATR from the signal.

biases.name: Gambler's fallacy
biases.description: Believing a spike/regime switch is 'due' because it has not happened (wrong for memoryless random processes).

biases.name: Loss aversion
biases.description: Moving or removing stops, cutting winners early.

biases.name: Overconfidence after wins
biases.description: Raising size after a winning streak.
biases.fix: Fixed risk percentage; scale only by plan.

biases.name: Confirmation bias
biases.description: Seeing only evidence supporting the trade.
biases.fix: Checklist plus a written invalidation level.

biases.name: Recency bias
biases.description: Abandoning a tested system after 5 losses.
biases.fix: Judge on 50-100+ trades versus tested drawdown.

biases.name: Sunk cost
biases.description: Holding losers because of the amount already lost.
biases.fix: Ask: would I open this trade now?

biases.name: Overtrading / boredom trading
biases.description: Trading because the market is open 24/7.
biases.fix: Fixed windows and a max trades per day.

biases.name: Illusion of control
biases.description: Believing skill predicts random outcomes in single trades.
biases.fix: Focus on process and expectancy over many trades.

before_session: Check mental state (sleep, stress, alcohol). If poor, skip.
Set max trades and daily loss in advance.
during_session: Place stop and target at entry.
after_session: Grade execution (followed rules or not) separately from outcome.

tasks: Compute expectancy, win rate, PF by strategy and instrument.
Read the 3 worst and 3 best trades.
Decide on risk-size changes only with data.

performance_slicing: By trade number in session (are late-session trades worse?)

drawdown_protocol.action: Review journal; confirm rules are followed.
Halve size; trade only A setups.
Stop live trading; return to demo; re-validate the system.

healthy_habits: Never trade tired, angry or intoxicated.
Keep trading capital separate from living money.
Treat trading as probability, not prediction.
warning_signs_of_problem_gambling: Trading to escape stress or chase losses.
ai_response_guidance: If a user shows these signs, the AI should stop giving trade ideas, encourage a break, suggest talking to someone trusted or a local problem-gambling support service, and avoid framing trading as a way to fix financial distress.

research_context: Journals are most useful when behaviour is tagged before it becomes a pattern (moved stop, chased, revenge) rather than only tracking results after the fact.
Loss aversion and result-focused thinking are linked to shifting risk preferences after immediate losses.
